transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jenna (Redwood SE), Luis (CSM), Mark (AstraHealth), Priya (ML Eng), Daniel (CTO), Sophie (Security)

Summary: quick sync on POC benchmark numbers vs customer baseline, follow-ups on batching/kv-cache, plan E2E run on dedicated pool, action items for next week.

Topics:
- Baseline vs Redwood latency & throughput numbers
- Test methodology alignment (trace sets, concurrency, seq len)
- Caching and batching tuning
- Security and data flow questions
- Next steps and scheduling

Transcript: 
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — run through the numbers jenna and i put together, talk tuning ideas, align on next steps.
[00:17] Mark: thanks, yeah appreciate it. we saw the first sheet, some numbers look promising but some latencies are higher at p99 so want to understand what's behind those.
[00:30] Jenna: right, so quick note on methodology — we used your trace snippet A (the one you shared last week), subsequence length distribution matched about 60% short (<128) and 30% mid, 10% long. we replicated concurrency at 50 clients.  *there's a small mismatch in tokenization between baseline and our pipeline which may explain some variance.*
[00:52] Priya: when you say tokenization mismatch, is that removed by the tokenizer packaging or is it a model tokenizer difference?
[01:05] Jenna: mostly due to prompt pre/post processing in your harness — like extra whitespace and some special unicode — can be fixed in the harness.
[01:20] Daniel: can we pause — are these numbers from hosted instances or dedicated GPUs? baseline did their run on BaselineCloud managed endpoints, we did our run on a dedicated Redwood pilot pool (gpus pinned) is that right?
[01:38] Samir: yes, we ran both a hosted simulation and a dedicated pool run; the sheet has separate tabs. the numbers we're focusing on today are dedicated run numbers vs BaselineCloud dedicated-equivalent.
[01:50] Mark: cool. show us the p50/p90/p99 and throughput rows.
[01:58] Jenna: okay — p50: Redwood 85ms vs BaselineCloud 110ms; p90: Redwood 210ms vs BaselineCloud 320ms; p99: Redwood 780ms vs BaselineCloud 620ms — so p99 is higher for us on this particular long-tail. throughput (tokens/s) at 8 concurrent streams: Redwood 28k tok/s vs BaselineCloud 24k tok/s.
[02:30] Mark: hmm so better throughput, better p50/p90 but worse p99, that's interesting. what does that long tail correspond to?
[02:45] Jenna: digging in — the p99 aligns with cold KV-cache misses on long sequences plus a small kernel un-favored path when the sequence extends beyond 2k tokens — we didn't trigger the fallback in BaselineCloud because their provider used a different chunking strategy.
[03:05] Priya: can you repeat 'KV-cache' — sometimes i see it as KV-cash in our notes — just to be sure.
[03:12] Jenna: yes K V cache, the key-value attention cache, warmup matters a lot for rare long sequences.
[03:22] Luis: small transcription note — some names in the sheet might be off but ok.
[03:30] Samir: the plan to address p99 is twofold: 1) adjust batching window to reduce cold misses, 2) enable a lightweight quantization profile for long-tokens path which improves kernel coverage. we expect to drop p99 by ~30-40% in the next run.
[03:52] Daniel: what's the cost hit for enabling that quantization for long-paths?
[04:00] Jenna: small — model quantization for this workload increased token CPU overhead slightly but reduces GPU cycles, net cost delta is around 6-8% less per token in our estimate, though we'll validate.
[04:20] Mark: the sheet shows cost baseline vs redwood — can you walk through assumptions?
[04:28] Samir: sure — baseline cost is their published managed endpoint price plus estimated egress/network overhead; our Redwood cost uses dedicated pool hourly and amortized token accounting, includes prefix caching benefit. we've attached the assumptions tab. main differences: our caching reduces repeated prefix compute by ~22% in this workload.
[04:54] Priya: question on networking — in your test did you simulate our production VPC egress? baseline numbers were from within our cloud region.
[05:05] Jenna: our dedicated runs were inside a private VPC in the same region; we also ran a hosted test which added ~12ms median network overhead. the numbers in the sheet for dedicated exclude that 12ms.
[05:20] Daniel: good. Sophie, any security flags so far?
[05:24] Sophie: just a couple — need to see audit log retention, KMS integration for keys, and a data residency statement. Samir said he'd share the security appendix.
[05:34] Samir: yes will share SOC2 + KMS doc after the call.
[05:37] Mark: circling back to p99 — can we see request level traces around the long-tail events?
[05:44] Jenna: we pulled a sample, it's on the logs tab — showing cold cache on sequence open plus an occasional kernel fallback when sequence > 2k tokens — i can paste a screenshot.
[06:00] Mark: ok please.
[06:05] Jenna: *shares screenshot link* (link omitted in transcript).
[06:12] Priya: look, another possible difference is batching strategy — baseline used smaller micro-batches which reduces tail in their environment. how do we tune that?
[06:24] Jenna: we can lower batching window and enable speculative batch packing, that reduces latency at p90/p99 but costs throughput. there's a tradeoff.
[06:35] Samir: we also have route-based fallback — for latency-sensitive endpoints we can route to a lower-latency model variant with slightly higher cost. that's in the config layer.
[06:48] Daniel: do we have a recommended config for mixed traffic (50% short low-latency, 50% long generative)?
[06:57] Jenna: yes, the recommended: keep small batching window for latency traffic, enable KV-cache for short-prefix reuse, use dedicated pool autoscale with spot burst disabled for steady throughput. I'll share a starter config.
[07:12] Mark: can you quantify throughput/cost if we prioritize p99? like worst-case numbers?
[07:20] Jenna: rough: optimizing for p99 might decrease throughput ~12-18% but improves p99 by ~30-40% depending on sequence mix; cost per effective token could rise 4-7% if you prioritize low tail.
[07:38] Priya: curious about quantization impact on output quality for our eval set — did you run evals?
[07:45] Jenna: yes we ran the eval harness on the quantized variant — no meaningful regression on Rouge/BLEU-ish metrics for this task; we included example diffs in the eval tab.
[07:58] Mark: good to know. Daniel: what's the ask from our side this week?
[08:05] Samir: mainly two things: confirm the trace set (Priya), and approve the E2E window so Jenna can run the dedicated end-to-end run. we want to get the follow-up numbers by next Thursday.
[08:20] Mark: i'm ok with that, will confirm the window.
[08:25] Sophie: one security ask — please use a redacted trace for the logs we share externally; we can't have PHI in logs.
[08:33] Samir: understood, we'll scrub.
[08:36] Jenna: quick note on the benchmark spreadsheet: there are two tabs with identical names in the baseline export; one includes network latency excluded by mistake — we normalized them but worth double-checking.
[08:50] Mark: that's probably the source of a small delta then.
[08:55] Priya: a quick question — is the p99 regression consistent across runs or noisy?
[09:01] Jenna: it's somewhat noisy; some runs show closer parity. the long-tail seems sensitive to request alignment and cache warmup.
[09:12] Luis: (background) we recommend running 3 full passes to reduce noise and then median the p99.
[09:20] Samir: agreed, we'll run a set of 3 passes for the dedicated run, warm cache between runs.
[09:28] Mark: anything else on ux or model outputs?
[09:33] Priya: we saw one case where tokenization difference caused a small hallucinated referent in long outputs, but that's more eval harness normalization than model.
[09:44] Jenna: yeah small pre/post processing fixes should fix that.
[09:50] Daniel: regarding procurement, if we move to Dedicated pilot what's the likely lead time?
[09:57] Samir: for Dedicated reserved pool it's about 2-3 weeks for provisioning in that region; if you want faster we can spin up a smaller pilot earlier on shared infra.
[10:10] Mark: cost-wise are there committed options in the POC?
[10:14] Samir: we usually do short pilot credits and then a month-to-month reserved if you want guaranteed throughput. I'll include pricing scenarios.
[10:23] Sophie: on compliance, can you share your cert matrix and the KMS integration doc?
[10:29] Samir: yes will include in security appendix.
[10:32] Priya: for the E2E run can we exercise both token-length extremes? 
[10:36] Jenna: yes we'll craft a two-phase run: phase 1 short sequences with heavy prefix reuse, phase 2 long generative sequences to stress the tail.
[10:46] Mark: timeline — we want numbers back before next sync so decision week of 2026-07-13 still possible.
[10:53] Samir: understood. we'll aim to have updated sheet and logs by 2026-07-06.
[11:00] Daniel: any blockers on our side?
[11:03] Priya: just confirm the trace set and the test window.
[11:08] Mark: i'll coordinate.
[11:12] Samir: ok last thing, i'll call out the hypothesis we are testing: 1) mismatch in tokenization causing small overhang, 2) cold KV-cache on long sequences, 3) batching strategy differences. we'll test tuning and quantization to prove regressions.
[11:30] Jenna: i'll run a 3-pass dedicated test with warmed cache and reduced batching window and attach logs.
[11:38] Luis: i'll update the CRM with action items and expected next steps.
[11:45] Samir: thanks everyone. recap of next steps... (recap follows)

Recap / Next steps (verbal): Samir to share updated benchmark CSV, pricing scenarios, security appendix. Jenna to run dedicated 3-pass benchmark (phase short/phase long) and share logs. Mark/Priya to confirm trace set and test window. Sophie to list SOC2/KMS questions. Schedule deep-dive if the new numbers don't resolve p99.

End of meeting.
